//devDependencies:@emnapi: task-104 / bug-063. @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime are NOT imported by anything in this repository. They are declared here, at the exact version the overrides block below pins, because an overrides pin binds a version but does not make npm record a node: under npm 11.x a plain `npm install` prunes both hoisted entries out of package-lock.json and reports `up to date`, which silently reverts task-080 and makes `npm ci` fail again under the npm 10.9.x that the pipeline's pinned Node 22.12.0 bundles (bug-056). A DIRECT dependency is never pruned, so declaring them is what makes the lock entries survive an ordinary install. Keep the two versions here equal to the overrides pins - `npm run check:lockfile` (scripts/check-lockfile-pins.cjs) fails if they drift, if either entry leaves the lock, or if these declarations are removed. Being devDependencies, they are never installed by a consumer of the published package.
//overrides: task-080 / bug-056 / dl-069 option (b). @napi-rs/wasm-runtime (dev, optional, reached through eslint -> @unrs/resolver) declares @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime as REQUIRED peers, and npm recorded no hoisted entry for either - so npm resolved them from the registry on every install and `npm ci` then rejected the lock for missing what it had just resolved. That is invisible under npm 11.x and fatal under the npm 10.9.0 that the pipeline's pinned Node 22.12.0 bundles, which is why it surfaced only in the release gate. These exact pins make both peers resolve from package-lock.json instead of the registry. Scoped to @napi-rs/wasm-runtime on purpose: the nested @emnapi/core@1.10.0 under @unrs/resolver-binding-wasm32-wasi is a different edge and stays where it is. Revisit on any eslint / @unrs/resolver bump; test/cli/lockfile-peer-overrides.test.ts fails if the lock stops carrying these. task-104 amends this: the overrides block alone did NOT keep the entries in the lock - see the //devDependencies:@emnapi note above.
